newsitem.title: UK: Pound tumbles after UK rate rise, Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: Pound tumbles after UK rate rise, Tietmeyer.

text.p: Sterling lost more than a pfennig against the German mark and about half a cent versus the dollar at Thursday's midsession after Britain's central bank raised its base rate 25 basis points to 6.75 percent.
But London stocks cut early losses on initial relief the expected rate increase was only a quarter point instead of the half point some analysts had forecast.

"This was entirely expected as far as the equity market is concerned," said SocGen strategist Andy Hartwill. "Maybe we can sit back for a while and wait for these rises to take effect. The market will like it a damned sight more than 50 basis points."
Others said the smaller rate rise was disheartening because it made the Bank of England (BOE) seem soft on inflation.

"I would have hoped that the Bank of England would roar but in fact, it hasn't," said Richard Jeffrey, chief economist at Charterhouse. "I think we will look back on these rate rises and conclude that (the BOE) was not aggressive enough...I think we'll eventually see the market come off."
Sterling and the dollar were already losing against the mark when the rate rise was announced because of earlier comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer.
The dollar's losses also pushed German and French shares down further into the red.
Tietmeyer said Germany's central bank was watching foreign exchange market developments closely and that the dollar's sharp rise against the mark was now over.
"We will naturally watch the developments in markets," he said. "You can be sure that it is important for us that the mark remains a strong currency, and we enter the euro as a strong currency."
The euro is the planned single European currency to be launched on January 1, 1999.
Tietmeyer also said: "I think the British pound very strongly reflects the domestic situation."
Tietmeyer's remarks also pressured German shares to session lows in active bourse trade as the dollar shed about half a pfennig against the mark.

Profit-taking in the 30-share DAX index also emerged as investors rushed to take profits after the Bundesbank said it was closely watching the DAX's recent sharp gains. The DAX scored a record high of 4,066.09 on Wednesday.
Tietmeyer said the DAX's surge did not reflect the health of the entire German economy.

In Paris, domestic appliance maker SEB SA was the biggest loser, sliding 5.16 percent to 1,067 French francs by 1150 GMT. Dealers noted SEB's continental Europe sales fell despite a 17-percent overall rise in first-half sales.

Among the gainers, wood, pulp and packaging company La Rochette jumped 7.58 percent to 24.85 francs. Although the company said it did not know why shares were sharply higher, dealers said a Credit Lyonnais study said the paper sector stood to gain in volume this year.
In metals markets, London gold was fixed at $319.65 per ounce, slightly higher than Wednesday's fix but slightly down from the closing price.

Dealers expected gold prices to drift up, recovering some of its losses to 12-year lows. "I think we have seen the lows, and the next move is toward $325" this week, a dealer at a major Swiss bank said.
But traders said sentiment remained bearish and heavy selling could reemerge next week.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was at 112.83 yen and 1.7540 marks compared with 112.97 and 1.7612 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 5.3 points at 4,757.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 63.48 points at 3,992.38.
PARIS - The CAC-40 dropped 18.90 points to 2,931.66.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $319.65 per ounce, compared with Wednesday's close of $319.75. Silver was set at $4.36, two cents higher than Wednesday's close at $4.34.
